# @orchestra-design-system/core

Stencil-based web components for the Orchestra design system.

This package is the source of truth for the design system’s UI primitives and web-component runtime. It provides framework-agnostic components built on web standards, with theme-aware styling and accessibility support.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @orchestra-design-system/core
```

## Quick start

```ts
import { defineCustomElements } from '@orchestra-design-system/core/loader'
import '@orchestra-design-system/themes/light.css'

defineCustomElements()
```

Then use the components in HTML:

```html
<orchestra-button text="Click me"></orchestra-button>
```

## Features

- Web Components built with Stencil
- Theme-aware styling via CSS variables generated by the themes package
- Framework wrappers for React, Vue, and Angular
- Accessibility-oriented component APIs
- TypeScript-first developer experience

## Theming

The core package consumes token values from the themes package. Import the public theme bundle in the consumer app or Storybook:

```css
@import '@orchestra-design-system/themes/light.css';
@import '@orchestra-design-system/themes/dark.css';
```

or in JavaScript:

```ts
import '@orchestra-design-system/themes/light.css'
```

## Component structure

```text
packages/core/
├── src/
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── button/
│   │   ├── icon/
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── helpers.ts
│   ├── index.ts
│   ├── types/
│   └── utils/
├── dist/
├── hydrate/
├── loader/
├── stencil.config.ts
├── package.json
├── readme.md
└── tsconfig.json
```

## Development

### Build

```bash
npm run build
```

### Watch mode

```bash
npm run start
```

### Test

```bash
npm run test
npm run test:spec
npm run test:e2e
```

## Notes

- The theme CSS bundle is owned by the themes package.
- The core package remains the source of UI implementation and Stencil runtime logic.
- Generated output targets include the loader and hydration entry points used by consumers.
